“We want to keep the Labour party in government doing good things and we need to wake up to that.” 

The Labour Party needs to “act quickly” and put together their messaging for the next two years or they “will end up like [their] colleagues in local government”, says Catherine West MP.

Catherine West was speaking to Carole Walker.  Listen live on Times Radio.

author: Times News
description:
After Labour’s heavy election losses, Keir Starmer is facing renewed questions over his leadership. The prime minister says he will not walk away, but some Labour MPs are already discussing who could come next.
Wes Streeting, Angela Rayner and Andy Burnham are among the names being talked about inside the party. But launching a challenge would not be simple. Under Labour rules, a candidate would need support from 80 MPs, and any contest could expose deep divisions between the party’s moderate and left-wing factions.
So who could replace Starmer, how would a leadership challenge work, and could he survive it?
